claim: World population on 1 July 2024 was 8,161,972,572 (8.16 billion); Asia 4,806,898,007, that is 58.9% of the world
source: UN DESA Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024, Demographic Indicators (medium variant)
page_or_section: columns TPopulation1July, Location=World and Asia, Time=2024
note: File values are in thousands. Shares computed by us.

claim: Eastern Asia (1,656,115,405) + South-Eastern Asia (695,149,428) + Southern Asia (2,064,056,491) = 4,415,321,324 people on 1 July 2024, 54.1% of the world; South Asia 25.3%, East Asia 20.3%, South-East Asia 8.5%
source: UN DESA Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024, Demographic Indicators (medium variant)
page_or_section: Locations Eastern Asia, South-Eastern Asia, Southern Asia, Time=2024
note: Our sum of three UN subregions as a stand-in for 'Monsoon Asia'. UN subregions include non-monsoon land (Mongolia, west China, arid western Pakistan), so 54% is an upper bound; the same regions were 52.2% in 1950 (claim 04). UN DESA does not define 'Monsoon Asia'.

claim: India (1,450,935,791) and China (1,419,321,278) together held 2,870,257,069 people on 1 July 2024, 35.2% of the world; Indonesia 283.5 million, Pakistan 251.3 million, Bangladesh 173.6 million, Viet Nam 101.0 million
source: UN DESA Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024, Demographic Indicators (medium variant)
note: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Philippines are in the monsoon belt (our grouping).

claim: In 1950 the same three UN regions had 1,300,537,920 people, 52.2% of a world of 2,493,092,848; Asia was 54.9%. So 'more than half the world lives in Monsoon Asia' was already true in 1950 and the share has barely changed; their number rose 3.4 times by 2024
source: UN DESA Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024, Demographic Indicators (medium variant)
note: Shows the claim is a long-run structural fact. 3.4x = 4,415.3 / 1,300.5 (our arithmetic).

claim: Premise check: Geen et al. (2020) say monsoons worldwide, taken together, influence 'over one third of the world's population'; the UN sum for East, South-East and South Asia is 54%, but that counts whole regions, not only people living in monsoon rain
value: one third (all monsoons, Geen) vs 54% (whole UN regions)
source: Geen R., Bordoni S., Battisti D., Hui K. (2020) Monsoons, ITCZs, and the concept of the global monsoon, Rev. Geophys. 58, e2020RG000700
note: Different measures: Geen counts people under any monsoon on Earth; the UN sum is three whole regions of Asia. In the answer say 'about half the world lives in the Asian monsoon belt'; do not pin a precise monsoon-only share.

claim: FAO: rice is the staple of Asia and central to the food security of about half of the world population; Asia accounts for more than 90 percent of world rice production and consumption; about 140 million rice-farming households
value: >90% of world rice; ~half of world population; 140 m households
source: FAO, A regional rice strategy for sustainable food security in Asia and the Pacific (RAP Publication 2014/05, Bangkok)
page_or_section: section 'Challenges and opportunities in regional rice sector development'
note: FAO's own wording of the 'rice feeds half the world' link the question assumes. Audit: FAOSTAT 2024 (claim 07) gives Asia 89.4% of production, so '>90 percent' is FAO's rounded figure; use 89.4% for a number on screen.

source: FAOSTAT, Crops and livestock products (Production_Crops_Livestock_E_All_Data_Normalized, file dated 23 Dec 2025), item Rice
page_or_section: Item=Rice, Elements Production and Area harvested, Year=2024, Area=Asia, World

claim: FAOSTAT 2024 rice production, million tonnes: India 217.9 (26.6% of world), China 209.2 (25.5%), Bangladesh 60.6 (7.4%), Indonesia 53.1 (6.5%), Viet Nam 43.5 (5.3%); these five make 71.2% of world rice
source: FAOSTAT, Crops and livestock products (Production_Crops_Livestock_E_All_Data_Normalized, file dated 23 Dec 2025), item Rice

claim: FAO: of Asia's 144 million ha of rice, about 60% is irrigated, 34% rainfed lowland (including coastal saline and deepwater) and 6% rainfed upland; so about 40% depends on rain alone
source: FAO, A regional rice strategy for sustainable food security in Asia and the Pacific (RAP Publication 2014/05, Bangkok)
page_or_section: 'Background' paragraph under the rice ecosystems heading
note: 40% rainfed is our sum (34 + 6). FAOSTAT 2023 Asia rice area was 144.3 Mha, matching FAO's 144 million ha.

value: rainfall instability a main rice risk
source: FAO, A regional rice strategy for sustainable food security in Asia and the Pacific (RAP Publication 2014/05, Bangkok)
page_or_section: risk paragraph beginning 'Rice farmers have to contend with multiple sources of risk'
note: Pairs with ledger M081 (SD about 10% of mean), M073-M074 (ENSO).

claim: IPCC AR6 WG1 Ch.8 defines the regional monsoon seasons used for trend work: South and Southeast Asian monsoon June-July-August-September (SAsiaM); East Asian monsoon June-July-August (EAsiaM); six regional monsoons in all
value: S/SE Asia JJAS; East Asia JJA
source: IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 8, final published PDF (ipcc.ch, 2021); saved copy is the Final Government Distribution draft (Do Not Cite)
page_or_section: Figure 8.11 caption (PDF p.41 of the final)
note: Audit fix: saved local copy is the draft, not the final; wording verified in the live final PDF. Gives the two sub-systems of Monsoon Asia with their season lengths. Ledger M084 covers the observed weakening.

claim: JMA: the East Asian 'Baiu' is a cloudy, rainy early-summer period lasting early June to late July in all of Japan except Hokkaido; Okinawa/Amami start and end about a month earlier. Climatological dates 1991-2020: Okinawa about 10 May to 21 June; Kanto/Koshin about 7 June to 19 July
value: Baiu early Jun - late Jul; Okinawa ~10 May-21 Jun
source: Japan Meteorological Agency, Climatological dates of Baiu onset and withdrawal
note: East Asian counterpart of India's onset-and-withdrawal pattern. Baiu is front-driven; contrast with India's convergence-zone monsoon is our gloss, not JMA's.
